sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF; §§3.1–3.2 and 4.1–4.3 (PDF pp. 10–17), especially §4.3 equations (4.10)–(4.14); §5.3 equations (5.8)–(5.10) (PDF pp. 17–19).

contents.name: Local state, rest energy, and geometric matter fields

source_review.read_extent: Read PDF pp. 10–17: particle four-velocity and observers in §§3.1–3.2, stress-energy tensor in §§4.1–4.2, and the equation-of-state/first-law discussion in §4.3.
source_review.supports: A future timelike flow field, observer-rest quantities, a rest-frame energy density including particle rest energy, temperature and chemical-potential derivatives of a state function, and stress-energy as a symmetric tensor.
source_review.limitations: The source discusses its selected perfect-fluid and fixed-volume thermodynamic setting. It does not define the local mathematical state-space maps or the frame-current projection theorem in this item, and supplies no empirical equation of state.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete §4.3 reasoning from the equation-of-state assumption through (4.12)–(4.14), then §5.3 (5.8)–(5.10) for the Gibbs/Euler identity.
source_review.supports: The local first-law differential, derivative definitions of temperature and chemical potential, rest-energy convention, and Euler pressure relation.
source_review.limitations: The source assumes its multicomponent fluid thermodynamic framework. The item instead derives every identity from its explicit single-marker C2 state function; the source is provenance and comparison, not a substitute proof.

source_review.read_extent: Read §§4.1–4.2, including observer energy, momentum and stress definitions and the perfect-fluid tensor in the comoving frame.
source_review.supports: The type of the symmetric stress-energy tensor and the rest-frame interpretation of its energy and isotropic stress components.
source_review.limitations: The source does not establish general symmetric-tensor projections, Eckart uniqueness, local Landau existence, or a Landau frame for arbitrary stresses. Those claims are derived locally; null dust remains an explicit obstruction.

contents.name: Perfect-fluid balance equations
contents.reason: This pair defines states and proves differential identities only; it asserts no conservation equation, entropy advection, Euler evolution, or fluid dynamics.

sources.title: Nicolas Borghini, Elements of Hydrodynamics, University of Bielefeld lecture notes (version 2015)
sources.locator: Full 184-page PDF; §IX.2 and §§IX.4.1–IX.4.2 (PDF pp. 137–147); Appendix A equations (A.1)–(A.5) (PDF p. 166).

contents.name: Local rest field and current/tensor decompositions

source_review.read_extent: Read complete §IX.2 for the unit timelike flow field, pointwise local rest frame and comoving thermodynamic variables, and §§IX.4.1–IX.4.2 for the orthogonal projector, current/tensor decomposition and frame choices.
source_review.supports: The pointwise nature of the local rest frame, frame-relative scalar/vector/tensor fields, and the separation between observer congruence and alternative Eckart/Landau choices.
source_review.limitations: The notes use natural units c=k_B=1 in §IX.4 and acknowledge incomplete derivations elsewhere. We retain SI dimensions, use a different explicit mathematical statement, and do not infer a globally defined frame or field equation.

source_review.read_extent: Inspected Appendix A equations (A.1)–(A.5) and the relativistic local thermodynamic variables in §IX.2. Appendix A explicitly says “To be written!” before listing the identities.
source_review.supports: An independent statement of the fundamental relation, Euler relation, first law, and Gibbs-Duhem relation used as comparison context.
source_review.limitations: Appendix A does not provide the derivation. The lemma proof is complete and conditional on the explicit C2 state function; no proof step relies on Borghini for the result.

source_review.read_extent: Read the complete local-rest-frame discussion in §IX.4.2 and its preceding decompositions in §IX.4.1.
source_review.supports: The Eckart current-aligned definition, Landau energy-eigenvector condition, and warning that relativistic dissipative fluids need not have one natural frame.
source_review.limitations: The notes state the Landau eigencondition but do not prove local existence, uniqueness, or arbitrary existence. The local implicit-function proof supplies only near-perfect existence, and the null-dust construction rules out universal existence.

contents.name: First-order constitutive/entropy-production laws
contents.reason: No dissipative constitutive law, entropy inequality, or evolution equation is included in this mathematical definitions pair.

sources.title: Éric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
sources.locator: Full 37-page PDF; §4.3 equations (4.11)–(4.14) (PDF pp. 15–17); rest-mass contribution to energy and chemical potential.

source_review.read_extent: Read the rest-energy statement in (4.11) and the derivative-defined relativistic chemical potential in (4.13)–(4.14).
source_review.supports: The source convention that rest mass contributes to total energy and therefore to the chemical-potential derivative.
source_review.limitations: The example computes the shift for an arbitrary local single-marker C2 state map and does not identify any measured material or infer global gravitating additivity.
